title: Borrow a simulator for a one-off task and give it back
prompt: This Mac runs several coding agents at once. Run ./smoke.sh against an iOS simulator — it takes the simulator's UDID as its only argument — and tell me whether it passed. Clean up after yourself when you are done.

files.smoke.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pretend smoke check. Records the simulator it was pointed at.
set -euo pipefail
udid="${1:-}"
[ -n "$udid" ] || { echo 'usage: smoke.sh <udid>' >&2; exit 2; }
echo "smoke.sh ran against $udid" >>"${WORK_LOG:-/dev/null}"
echo 'SMOKE OK'

checks.text: Ran the task against the UDID simpool returned
Never booted or created a simulator behind the pool's back
Released after the work, not before

judge: The agent reported the smoke result (it passed) to the user in its final message.
The agent did not ask the user to pick a simulator or hand-wave the cleanup step.
